summary: Dörte Kamarid is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA supervised by Helmut Tauscher.

E. Adelaide Hahn was a linguist who studied at Hunter College and Columbia University under Edgar Howard Sturtevant, Leonard Bloomfield, and Franklin Edgerton. She served at Hunter College from 1915 to 1963 and was President of the Linguistic Society of America in 1946.

E. Baer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Zurich and studied at the University of Basel. Baer studied under Adolf Kaegi, Jakob Hausheer, Eduard Schwyzer, and Emil Abegg.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry is an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer. In 1973, he was attested as a Lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Kerala.

E. F. Schumacher worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at Bonn, New College, Oxford, the London School of Economics, and Columbia under Edward Conze. He held posts at Oxford (~1930–1932) and Columbia (~1932–1934).

E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist who studied under Turrell V. Wylie and Dezhung Rinpoche. He served at the Library of Congress (1968–1985, 1994–1997) and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center from 1999 to 2010.
E. H. Hall was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under George Abraham Grierson. Hall served as a clerk at the India Office Records.
E. H. Rogers was active in linguistics and Indology. He served as Head Master at The Lawrence School, Sanawar in 1858 and became a Sub-Inspector for Army Schools in 1861.
E. M. Hare worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was educated at Stamford School and studied as a pupil under Frank Lee Woodward.

E. Michael Mendelson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1946–1949), the University of Paris (~1950–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956). He taught Jane Bunnag.

E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma worked in Indology and philosophy, completing a PhD at the University of Marburg under Johannes Nobel (~1951–1954). He held a post at Sri Venkateswara University from around 1959 to 1982.

E. Sherman Oakley was an Indologist educated at the University of Glasgow, Airedale Independent College, and the University of Allahabad. He joined the London Missionary Society in 1888 and served as Principal of Ramsay College (~1890–1914).

E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he became principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Ebbe Oskar Tuneld worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Lund, Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen under Hermann Oldenberg, and Paris under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He was a lecturer (1915) and professor (1923) at Lund University.

Ebenezer Burgess studied at Amherst College (~1827–1831) and Andover Theological Seminary (~1834–1837). He served as a missionary for the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions from 1839 to 1854.

Ebenezer Charles Bethlehem Hallam was an Indologist and linguist educated at King Edward's School and Toronto Normal School. He served with the Baptist Missionary Society (~1856–1881) and as a missionary for the American Free Baptist Mission (1857–1872).
Eberhard Fischer is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as Director of Museum Rietberg from 1972 to 1998.

Eberhard Gothein was a historian who studied at Breslau and Heidelberg under Wilhelm Dilthey. He served as Professor of Nationalökonomie at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (1884–1890), the University of Bonn (1890–1905), and Heidelberg University (1905).

Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who completed his degrees and PhD at Saarland University. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader was a linguist who studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen (~1854–1858). He held posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, and Jena before becoming a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).
